Same 640 test tasks for all methods; all trainable methods trained from fresh Qwen3.5 students for 100 learner updates x 64 episodes, equal domain mixture, by reverse-KL OPD from the same frozen Qwen3.8-27B teacher (except CAMP-I, task rewards), so systems differ only in memory mechanism. Baselines: frozen students and four memory-learning methods. Ablations of interface and supervision. Repetitions: one training seed per method in main table; five seeds for CAMP-II-4B only. Human intervention: none

CAMP-II-4B highest average (64.6% vs 54.2% CAMP-I and 51.8% best OPD baseline MemOPD w/ SFT); claimed 2.97x the gain of the strongest OPD baseline over the frozen student; 9B reaches 66.5%, closing 63% of the student-teacher gap. Replacing file interface by memory tools or compaction costs 16-17 points. Transfer: CAMP-II-4B +6.9 points over Qwen3.5-4B on both external suites. No significance tests

Distinguished methods clearly on CAMG-II; seed robustness shown only for CAMP-II-4B (SD 0.5); memory interventions (intact/shuffled/removed) support causal role of memory content. Limitations of comparison not discussed beyond scale
